issues.detail: Hebrew 'יְאֹרֵי מָצוֹר' means 'the canals/streams of Egypt' (or 'of the siege'), not '城邑的溪' (streams of the city). 'מָצוֹר' here likely refers to Egypt (Mizraim) or a fortified place, not 'city' generally. The Chinese renders it as '城邑的溪' which changes the referent.
Hebrew 'סוּף' in 'קָנֶה וָסוּף' means 'reed' (papyrus/rush), not '紅海' (Red Sea). The phrase is 'reed and rush' (both plants), not 'reeds and the Red Sea'. This is a significant mistranslation.
